paragraphs: Here's the point, friend: we have a high priest, and He is Jesus. He sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in heaven, and He ministers in the true tabernacle set up by the Lord, not by man (Hebrews 8:1-2). The earthly place was only a copy and shadow of what is in heaven (Hebrews 8:5). A cookie's shadow on the wall looks great, but I've never once been fed by it, and Jesus is the real thing.

Now look at what the new covenant gives. God says, "I will put My laws in their minds and inscribe them on their hearts. And I will be their God, and they will be My people" (Hebrews 8:10). It's not about getting every rule right from the outside anymore. God Himself works on the inside, and all of them will know Him, "from the least of them to the greatest" (Hebrews 8:11). Friend, that means nobody has to earn a seat at the table.

And then the line I'd stamp on every cookie box in this bakery: "For I will forgive their iniquities and will remember their sins no more" (Hebrews 8:12). The first covenant was a shadow and it's fading away, but this one rests on better promises (Hebrews 8:6, 13). So when you feel like the one who keeps messing up the batch, hear this: your sins are forgiven and remembered no more. Keep your ovens warm, baker, because you belong to a God who keeps His promises.
